_meta.status: v0 built from the public catalog snapshot because the Shopify export has not arrived. Replace it from HLR's export when it lands (Brand Review v2 question 5; owner HLR; Review 1). Ruled by Eddie 2026-10-18: display names (Q10; Gate 2 call 4 a) and keys (Gate 2 call 7 a). Ruled by Eddie 2026-10-22: the derived fields kind and family, as built (Gate 2 package call 14).
_meta.built_by: lane D, Pack v0 structure side (Step 2)

source.origin: https://highlightrituals.com/products.json, the public storefront feed (182 published products)
source.snapshot_header: HLR catalog snapshot, 2026-10-17. Source: https://highlightrituals.com/products.json (public storefront, 182 published products). Provenance: observed. Names, prices and tags are verbatim from the store, including its dashes; the house rule on dashes applies to what we write, not to source data. price_usd is the variant range; skus counts variants that carry a SKU. Not the product database: Step 2 builds that from a client export.

_meta.keys: Ruled (Gate 2 call 7 a, Eddie, 2026-10-18): Shopify product handles until HLR's export lands, then SKUs with the handle kept as a field. Handles, not SKUs, because the snapshot is product-level: 549 of 650 variants carry a SKU and it keeps one example per product (observed.sku_example). A brief's "sku" for HLR is the handle until the export supplies variant SKUs; brief_lint.js and sku_lookup.js match on these keys.
_meta.how_to_read: Never wholesale. Resolve with skills/email-copy/scripts/sku_lookup.js --pack <pack> --match "<name or handle>". sku_lookup returns name, category, description, ingredients, nutrition and badges only; the observed block never reaches a writer.

fields.name: [derived by ruled rules] the house-style display name copy uses: a dash and a stone tail become "in" (Q10, DECISIONS 2026-10-17); a title with no dash is unchanged; a non-stone tail drops where the head names one product (Gate 2 call 4 a, DECISIONS 2026-10-18). name_status says which rule applied.
fields.shopify_title: [observed] the Shopify title verbatim, dashes included. Source data, never copy.
fields.name_status: which rule produced name: ruled, unchanged or proposed.
fields.category: [observed] the Shopify product type verbatim (two are wrong at source; see flags).
fields.kind: [documented] jewelry, crystal, ritual kit, packaging, service, service with jewelry, or jewelry with a service, from the type and title words (Session, Intensive, Message Add-On, Energy Reading, Gift Bag). (ratified 2026-10-22 by Eddie, Gate 2 package call 14)
fields.family: [documented] a product line read from a title pattern, kept only where two or more products share it; null otherwise. Feeds concrete_lexicon.product_families (lane C). (ratified 2026-10-22 by Eddie, Gate 2 package call 14)
fields.description: empty: the snapshot carries no product copy. Named gap; the export's Body HTML fills it.
fields.ingredients: [observed] materials the Shopify title itself names: a stone tail, an "in X" material the catalog confirms as a stone, tag or metal, or "The X Palm Stone" / "The X Point". Words that are not confirmed materials (Siren, Queen Conch) stay out. Option metals are not copied here.
fields.nutrition: null: not applicable to this catalog.
fields.badges: empty: no badge is sourced. Badges license figures in sku_lookup.js, so nothing goes here without a source.
fields.observed: [observed] storefront values verbatim from the snapshot: price ranges, variants, availability, publish date, options and tags. Reference only: no writer reads them.
fields.attributes: [observed] a birth month or zodiac sign the title names.
fields.flags: defects and open questions on the record, each with its source.

_meta.figures: This database licenses no figure. sku_lookup.js draws allowed figures from description, badges and nutrition, which are empty or null. Prices are observed storefront values for reference; copy carries prices, percentages, thresholds and codes as merge tokens ({{ ... }}) until HLR's export confirms them. Karat and metal statements follow _meta.brand_facts (metal_and_karat_statements) and the karat question at Review 1.
_meta.claims_note: Observed tags include intention words (Calm, Protection, Love, Emotional balance, Vitality and others). They are store data, not facts copy may state: benefit and health-adjacent language waits for C2; there is no claims ledger (DECISIONS 2026-10-31), so a benefit is sourced or not written, and the voice contract frames meaning as tradition or intention.

gaps.gap: Variant SKUs, barcodes and inventory: 101 of 650 variants carry no SKU in the public feed and the snapshot keeps one example per product.
Product descriptions (Body HTML): description is empty on every record, so no product prose is verifiable.
Prices confirmed by HLR: observed storefront ranges only; copy uses merge tokens.
Metals and karat by variant (14K Solid Gold, 14K Gold Filled, Sterling Silver, 14K Rose Gold seen in options) and the karat and origin claims in paid.
Re-key by SKU when the export lands, the handle kept as a field (Gate 2 call 7 a).
Source defects to fix in Shopify: 2 type mismatches, 6 stale handles, 3 copied stone tags, "Gold FIlled" casing, 80 dashed titles.
Services sold as products (sessions, readings): positioning and claims (C2).
Pack shots per product (pack_shot_index): imagery waits for usage rights (rule 8).

brand_facts._note: Brand and product facts that lived only in the retired claims ledger (lane C's seed, v0.2.0, archived under _archive/brand-pack/), moved here with their wording and sources on 2026-10-31 (DECISIONS 2026-10-31: the legal regime is deleted, every product fact keeps its source). Each fact is what its source says, not a fact HLR has confirmed: status says which, and the gap stays open until HLR confirms it. Copy states one only as the source states it. The ledger file is archived under _archive/brand-pack/.
brand_facts.dropped_rows: HLR-H01, HLR-H02, HLR-H03, HLR-F01, HLR-M01, HLR-M02, HLR-M04, HLR-M05: claim-pattern rows carrying a legal posture and counts of the claims live copy makes, no product fact. The observation that live copy makes health, anxiety and fertility claims stays in brand-context.md (Sensitive territory).
